summary: EBR (Escrowed Batch Reveal) effectively reduces first-proposal bias from 73.3% (HardGate) to 24.4%, a 48.9 percentage point reduction (p < 0.001). The result satisfies the pre-registered Accept/Proceed criterion (C <= B - 0.20) with zero completion rate drop. EBR's rank distribution is statistically indistinguishable from uniform (chi-squared p = 0.49), confirming that sequential visibility is the primary mechanism driving first-proposal bias in agentic marketplaces.
analysis: Four experimental conditions were compared on gemini-2.5-flash across 3 scenarios x 10-15 runs each. SoftWait (A) and ITS (A') both showed 63.3% earliest-arrival rates, matching Magentic's reported bias range. HardGate (B), which gates payment but reveals proposals sequentially, showed even higher bias at 73.3%. EBR (C), which buffers proposals and reveals them simultaneously in shuffled order, reduced the rate to 24.4% -- below the theoretical random chance of 33.3%. The primary comparison (B vs C) yields z = -4.639, p = 0.000002 (one-sided), with Fisher's exact confirming at p = 0.000003. The 95% CI for the difference (C - B) is (-0.669, -0.309), entirely below zero. Completion rates are 100% for all conditions, so EBR introduces no cost to task completion. The chi-squared test against uniform distribution yields p = 0.49, confirming the rank distribution under EBR is not significantly different from random. Secondary comparisons show neither SoftWait nor ITS significantly reduce bias compared to HardGate (p = 0.18 for both). This demonstrates that prompt-based and inference-time scaling interventions are insufficient -- a protocol-level change (batched reveal) is required.
reason: Verdict is 'good' because: (1) All four conditions ran successfully to completion, producing both main and baseline results -- not 'failed'. (2) The proposed EBR method shows a large, statistically significant improvement over the primary baseline (HardGate): earliest-arrival rate drops from 73.3% to 24.4% (delta = 48.9pp, p < 0.001). (3) The pre-registered Accept/Proceed criterion is met: EarliestArrival(C) = 0.244 <= 0.533 = EarliestArrival(B) - 0.20, with zero completion rate drop. (4) EBR eliminates first-proposal bias entirely (rank distribution indistinguishable from uniform). (5) The effect is robust across all three scenario orderings. This constitutes strong evidence that sequential visibility is a causal driver of residual first-proposal bias, and EBR is an effective protocol intervention.
